evals.name: positive-trigger-critique
evals.prompt: Here's my 12-week plan for migrating the clinic's records to the new EHR (attached). Critique this plan and find weaknesses in my plan before I take it to the director.
evals.expected_output: The skill fires. It reads the whole plan, establishes the yardstick (goal, deadline reality, resources), runs all nine lenses, applies dominant repairs, and puts owner-held forks (e.g. big-bang vs phased cutover, what slips if the deadline holds) through batched option-picker rounds until resolved or stopped. Delivers a verdict line first, findings by severity, then the full revised plan under a decision ledger.

evals.name: positive-trigger-thai
evals.prompt: นี่คือแผนอ่านหนังสือเตรียมสอบบอร์ดจิตเวช 6 เดือนของผม ช่วยวิจารณ์แผนและปรับแผนให้ดีขึ้นหน่อย
evals.expected_output: The skill fires on the Thai trigger phrases (วิจารณ์แผน / ปรับแผน). Same procedure: yardstick (exam date, hours available), nine lenses — verifiability usually bites here (activities, not outcomes, as milestones) — batched interview on forks like breadth vs depth of coverage, then verdict + revised plan, register matching the user's Thai–English code-switching.

evals.name: negative-no-plan-exists
evals.prompt: Plan my study schedule for the psychiatry boards — six months out, working full time.
evals.expected_output: Does not fire. No plan exists to critique — this is a request to draft one, which hits the 'Not for drafting a plan from a bare goal' clause. The request routes through intent-lock for alignment, the plan gets drafted, and plan-critique is offered on the draft afterwards.

evals.name: negative-mid-task-decisions
evals.prompt: While you're refactoring, don't keep pinging me — collect your questions and ask me everything at once.
evals.expected_output: Does not fire. These are the agent's own mid-task execution decisions inside a locked goal — decision-interview owns the batched sweep-and-ask there. No existing plan artifact is being critiqued.

evals.name: negative-code-review
evals.prompt: Critique this Python script and tell me how to improve it.
evals.expected_output: Does not fire. The object is code, not a plan — 'Not for reviewing code or prose'. A code review proceeds outside this skill; plan-critique would only apply to a plan about the code (e.g. a refactoring roadmap), not the source itself.

evals.name: negative-execute-the-plan
evals.prompt: Here's the migration plan we agreed on — go ahead and execute it.
evals.expected_output: Does not fire. The user asked for execution, not judgment. Work proceeds on the plan as written; forks that execution surfaces are swept and batched by decision-interview, not re-critiqued here.
